page: Microsoft Azure HB120-16rs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the HBv3 server family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel processor and provides a substantial memory capacity of 456.0 GB, yielding 28.5 GB of RAM per core.

For storage-intensive workloads, the server includes 2412 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. It is also RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) capable, facilitating high-throughput, low-latency networking. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this instance.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 28.5 GB per core and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers a specialized hardware profile. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound tasks and large-scale database operations that require high-speed local NVMe storage without the overhead of excessive vCPU licensing costs. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive databases, in-memory analytics, and high-performance computing tasks requiring RDMA.
description: Microsoft Azure HB120-16rs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server within the HBv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor, paired with 456.0 GB of system memory, which translates to an exceptionally high allocation of 28.5 GB of RAM per core. The server is equipped with 2412 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. Additionally, it is RDMA capable, enabling low-latency networking for clustered environments. With no integrated GPUs, this server is designed for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU allocation make it qualitatively cost-efficient for resource-dense applications. It is highly suitable for large-scale databases, in-memory data processing, and high-performance computing workloads that benefit from RDMA and fast local storage.
